title: Set safe work zones
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Set up signs, barriers and ventilation that keep exits and fire equipment clear.
Control slip, trip and pedestrian hazards in a wet or occupied work area.
Remove the controlled work zone and restore access only after inspection.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Use signs, barriers, ventilation and traffic management appropriate to the work and site.

instruction.heading: Purpose and learning outcome
instruction.body: After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate set safe work zones in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

instruction.heading: Detailed workplace method
instruction.body: Plan equipment placement, safe access routes, wet-floor controls, ventilation, chemical handling and separation from occupants. Keep exits and fire equipment clear. Secure cords and hoses against trips and prevent public entry to wet or hazardous zones using the site-approved barriers. Avoid moving customer valuables and ensure tools do not damage walls, floors or furniture. Adjust barriers as the job progresses.

instruction.heading: Safety, boundaries and escalation
instruction.body: Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

instruction.heading: Worked example
instruction.body: An occupied corridor needs mopping during office hours. The team works in short sections, diverts pedestrians, dries each area and restores access only after inspection.

instruction.heading: Supervised practical
instruction.body: Mark up a floor plan showing staging, wet work, pedestrians and exits; then demonstrate setting up and removing a controlled work zone.

instruction.heading: Assessment and corrective feedback
instruction.body: An assessor observes the learner and verifies: Maintains clear exits, controls slips and trips, protects customer property and adapts controls during work. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

Plan equipment placement, safe access routes, wet-floor controls, ventilation, chemical handling and separation from occupants. Keep exits and fire equipment clear. Avoid moving customer valuables and ensure tools do not damage walls, floors or furniture. Adjust barriers as the job progresses.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Confirm the actual work scope, the hazards and who can authorise changes before setting up.
Plan equipment placement, safe access routes, wet-floor controls, ventilation and separation from occupants.
Keep exits and fire equipment clear throughout the job.
Secure cords and hoses against trips, and use site-approved barriers to keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones.
Avoid moving customer valuables, and make sure tools do not damage walls, floors or furniture.
In occupied areas, work in short sections and divert pedestrians around the work.
Adjust barriers as the job progresses.
Restore access only after the work zone has been inspected, and record the facts.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Exits and fire equipment stay clear throughout the job.
Wet-floor controls and site-approved barriers keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones.
Cords and hoses are secured against trips, and customer valuables are not moved.
Access is restored only after the work zone has been inspected.
summary: Signs, barriers, ventilation and traffic management are set up to suit the work and the site.
Exits and fire equipment are kept clear, cords and hoses are secured, and public entry to wet or hazardous zones is prevented.
The controlled zone is removed, and access is restored only after inspection.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which evidence or checks are essential when you set safe work zones?
options: Whether the public can use the wet area while you finish and whether they are allowed to take photos
Whether the cords can run across the walkway, if they are taped and whether the cords are long enough for the room
Exits, fire equipment, access routes, wet-floor controls and barriers, and ventilation planned before work starts
The number of buckets on the trolley and the brand and colour of the trolley and its wheels

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do with the barriers when a wet area cannot be made safe in time?
options: Restore access before inspection so the building is not disrupted
Keep the zone open to the public and warn them verbally while the work goes on
Pause, keep the zone closed, and reassess the barriers before restoring access
Move the barriers to suit the people walking by and leave the wet floor open

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a wet corridor be worked in an occupied building?
options: Work in short sections, divert pedestrians, dry each area and restore access only after inspection
Close the building for the rest of the day and tell all the staff to go home early today
Mop the whole corridor at once to finish sooner and leave the doors open to the street
Leave the wet floor unmarked, since people can see it and nobody needs to be told about it

knowledgeChecks.question: Which work-zone practice is unsafe in a wet area?
options: Using site-approved barriers around wet floors
Keeping exits and fire equipment clear
Leaving a wet area unmarked while the work continues
Securing cords and hoses against trips

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be recorded before a controlled work zone is reopened?
options: Note the zone only in your head and assume the crew will remember it for later on the day
Record the inspection before access is restored, and escalate any zone that cannot be kept safe
Barriers need a note only if a visitor was delayed and then the note goes in the diary
Restore access as soon as the mop dries and skip the inspection to save time on the job
